mcqs.stem: Best guess: an NFP's board votes to set aside $1 million of unrestricted cash as a 'board-designated endowment.' How are those net assets classified?

choices.explanation: Only donors create donor restrictions.
The board, not a donor, made the designation.
Correct. Board designations are internal and reversible.
A designation creates no obligation to an outside party.

mcqs.explanation: Board-designated amounts remain net assets **without donor restrictions**; they may be disclosed or shown separately within that class.

mcqs.stem: A donor gave $80,000 restricted to research. During the year the NFP spent $30,000 on research. How is the $30,000 reported?

choices.text: As an expense in net assets with donor restrictions
choices.explanation: Expenses are always reported in net assets without donor restrictions.

choices.text: No entry until the full $80,000 has been spent
choices.explanation: Releases occur as the purpose is fulfilled.

choices.text: As a reduction of the contribution revenue
choices.explanation: Revenue was properly recognized when the gift was received.

choices.text: A $30,000 release and research expense without restrictions
choices.explanation: Correct. The restriction is satisfied and the expense is unrestricted.

mcqs.explanation: Reclassify $30,000 from with to without donor restrictions (net assets released), and report the $30,000 research expense in the without-donor-restrictions column.

mcqs.stem: Which statement is required for all NFPs but has no direct counterpart for business entities?

choices.text: Analysis of expenses by function and nature
choices.explanation: Correct. All NFPs must present it (as a statement, on the face, or in notes).
Businesses present one too.
NFPs do not present OCI in that format.

choices.text: Statement of changes in stockholders' equity
choices.explanation: NFPs have no stockholders.

mcqs.explanation: ASU 2016-14 requires every NFP to provide an analysis of expenses by both functional and natural classification.

mcqs.stem: Which item is reported as a change in net assets **with** donor restrictions?

choices.text: A cash gift the donor stipulated must be used next year
choices.explanation: Correct. A time restriction makes it with donor restrictions until next year.
Expenses are reported only in net assets without donor restrictions.

choices.text: Board-designated funds for a future building
choices.explanation: Board designations are without donor restrictions.
Unrestricted revenue is without donor restrictions.

mcqs.explanation: Donor-imposed time or purpose restrictions create net assets with donor restrictions. Expenses and board designations never do.

mcqs.stem: An NFP received $500,000 in cash restricted by the donor to construct a building. The building was completed and placed in service this year at a cost of $500,000. Absent other stipulations, when is the restriction released?

choices.explanation: The purpose has not yet been met at receipt.

choices.text: Over the building's useful life as it is depreciated
choices.explanation: Absent a donor stipulation, the release occurs when placed in service, not over the life.

choices.text: When the building is placed in service
choices.explanation: Correct. That satisfies the purpose restriction.

choices.text: Never — building gifts are perpetually restricted
choices.explanation: Only endowment-type stipulations are perpetual.

mcqs.explanation: Gifts restricted to acquire long-lived assets are released when the asset is placed in service, unless the donor stipulates how long the asset must be used.

mcqs.stem: During the year an NFP had: unrestricted contributions $700,000; restricted contributions $200,000; releases from restriction $150,000; total expenses $820,000. What is the change in net assets **without** donor restrictions?

choices.explanation: This omits the releases, which increase unrestricted net assets.
This includes restricted contributions.
This includes restricted contributions and omits releases (900,000 − 820,000).

mcqs.explanation: Without donor restrictions: 700,000 + releases 150,000 − expenses 820,000 = **+30,000**. (With donor restrictions: 200,000 − 150,000 = +50,000.)

mcqs.stem: Which expense is classified as a **supporting activity** in an NFP's statement of activities?

choices.text: Cost of meals served at a homeless shelter
choices.explanation: Direct mission activity — a program service.
Correct. Accounting is management and general — a supporting activity.

choices.text: Scholarships awarded by an education foundation
choices.explanation: Awarding scholarships is the mission — program services.

choices.text: Vaccines administered at a free clinic
choices.explanation: Direct program service.

mcqs.explanation: Supporting activities are management and general (administration, accounting, governance) and fundraising. Mission-delivery costs are program services.

mcqs.stem: How must an NFP report investment return in its statement of activities?

choices.text: Gross, with investment expenses shown as management and general
choices.explanation: ASU 2016-14 requires netting external and direct internal investment expenses.

choices.text: Net of external and direct internal investment expenses
choices.explanation: Correct. Investment return is presented net of external and direct internal investment expenses; disclosure of those netted expenses is no longer required.

choices.text: Only realized gains; unrealized gains go to a separate equity account
choices.explanation: NFPs report realized and unrealized gains in the statement of activities.
Investment return is reported in the statement of activities.

mcqs.explanation: Investment return is presented net of external and direct internal investment expenses; disclosure of those netted expenses is no longer required.

mcqs.stem: An NFP's statement of financial position shows cash $300,000; receivables due in 6 months $120,000; investments $900,000 of which $600,000 is perpetual endowment corpus; and a pledge receivable restricted to next year's program $80,000. Ignoring expected releases, what financial assets are available for general expenditures within one year?

choices.explanation: Correct. 300,000 + 120,000 + (900,000 − 600,000) = 720,000; the restricted pledge is excluded.
This includes the endowment corpus and the restricted pledge.
This includes the restricted pledge.
This excludes all investments, including $300,000 that are not restricted.

mcqs.explanation: Available = cash 300,000 + current receivables 120,000 + unrestricted investments 300,000 = **720,000**. Perpetually restricted corpus and purpose-restricted pledges are excluded.

mcqs.stem: An NFP using the direct method in its statement of cash flows:

choices.text: Must also present the indirect-method reconciliation
choices.explanation: ASU 2016-14 removed this requirement for NFPs.

choices.text: Must present operating cash flows by net asset class
choices.explanation: Cash flows are not presented by net asset class.

choices.text: Is not required to present the indirect-method reconciliation
choices.explanation: Correct. NFPs may use the direct or indirect method; if direct, the reconciliation of change in net assets to operating cash flows is not required (ASU 2016-14).
All three categories are required.

mcqs.explanation: NFPs may use the direct or indirect method; if direct, the reconciliation of change in net assets to operating cash flows is not required (ASU 2016-14).

mcqs.stem: Which classification describes a donor's gift of $1,000,000 that must be invested forever, with income available for any purpose?

choices.text: Without donor restrictions, because the income is unrestricted
choices.explanation: The corpus is restricted in perpetuity.
Correct. The corpus is a perpetual donor restriction; income, when appropriated, is without restrictions.
The donor, not the board, imposed the restriction.
An unconditional gift is revenue, not a liability.

mcqs.explanation: Donor-restricted endowment corpus is reported in net assets with donor restrictions. Earnings are reported with donor restrictions until appropriated for expenditure (per state law, e.g., UPMIFA), then released.

mcqs.stem: An NFP spent $40,000 of unrestricted resources on a youth program for which it also holds a $25,000 donor-restricted gift for the same program. Absent donor instructions, how much is released from restriction?

choices.explanation: When an expense meets a restriction, the restriction is considered satisfied even if unrestricted resources were used first.
This subtracts the gift from the spending; the release equals the restricted amount satisfied.
Correct. Qualifying expenses of $40,000 fully satisfy the $25,000 restriction.
Only $25,000 was restricted.

mcqs.explanation: If an expense is incurred for a purpose for which both restricted and unrestricted resources are available, the donor restriction is treated as fulfilled to the extent of the expense. Release = lesser of the restriction (25,000) and qualifying expense (40,000).

mcqs.stem: Which is **not** a required financial statement (or equivalent presentation) for a private NFP?

choices.explanation: This is one of the required NFP presentations, so it is not the answer.

choices.text: Statement of changes in fund balances by fund
choices.explanation: Correct. That is a governmental concept; NFPs report by net asset class, not funds.
This is one of the required NFP presentations, so it is not the answer.
This is one of the required NFP presentations, so it is not the answer.

mcqs.explanation: Required NFP presentations: statement of financial position, statement of activities, statement of cash flows, and the analysis of expenses by function and nature. Fund-based statements belong to governments.

mcqs.stem: A not-for-profit received a $500,000 cash gift that the donor restricted to its permanent endowment. How is it reported in the statement of cash flows?

choices.explanation: Only contributions without long-term restrictions are operating.
The gift is a financing inflow; investing the cash later is investing.
The gift was received in cash.
Correct. Contributions restricted for long-term purposes, such as endowment, are financing inflows (ASC 230-10-45-14).

mcqs.explanation: NFP cash flows: contributions restricted to endowment, land, buildings or equipment are financing.

mcqs.stem: A draft NFP statement of cash flows (indirect method) starts with the change in net assets of $300,000, which includes a $40,000 unrealized gain on investments and a $100,000 cash gift restricted to building construction. What is net cash from operating activities if there are no other adjustments?

choices.explanation: Correct. 300,000 − 40,000 unrealized gain − 100,000 long-term restricted gift (a financing inflow) = 160,000.
This makes neither adjustment.
This removes the gain but leaves the restricted gift in operating activities.
This adds both items instead of subtracting them.

mcqs.explanation: Remove noncash gains, and reclassify contributions restricted for long-term purposes to financing activities.

mcqs.stem: Which not-for-profit entities must present an analysis of expenses by both nature and function?

choices.text: Only voluntary health and welfare entities
choices.explanation: The requirement was extended to all NFPs.
Correct. ASU 2016-14 requires all NFPs to present this analysis.

choices.text: Only NFPs with revenue over $1 million
choices.explanation: No size threshold applies.

choices.text: Only NFPs that receive federal grants
choices.explanation: The requirement applies to all NFPs.

mcqs.explanation: ASC 958-720-45-15: all NFPs report an analysis of expenses by function and nature in one location (a statement, the notes, or the face of the statement of activities).

mcqs.stem: What liquidity information must an NFP disclose?

choices.explanation: Forecasts aren't required.

choices.text: Its credit rating and borrowing capacity only
choices.explanation: Availability of financial assets is required.
Correct. NFPs disclose qualitative and quantitative information about liquidity and availability.
Availability includes other financial assets and limits on use.

mcqs.explanation: ASC 958-210-50: disclose quantitative information about financial assets available to meet cash needs for general expenditures within one year and qualitative information on liquidity management.

mcqs.stem: An NFP mails a brochure that asks for donations and also educates the public about its health program. When may it allocate the joint costs between fundraising and program?

choices.text: Whenever any program content is included
choices.explanation: All three criteria are required.

choices.text: Never; joint costs are always fundraising
choices.explanation: Allocation is allowed when the criteria are met.

choices.text: Only if a donor requires allocation
choices.explanation: Donor preference isn't the test.

choices.text: When purpose, audience and content tests are met
choices.explanation: Correct. All three criteria must be met; otherwise all costs are fundraising.

mcqs.explanation: ASC 958-720-45-29: if the purpose, audience and content criteria are met, joint costs are allocated; otherwise they are reported as fundraising.

mcqs.stem: An NFP spends $80,000 on a program for which a donor had restricted a prior-year gift. How is the restriction release reported?

choices.explanation: Correct. Expenses are reported there.

choices.text: As new revenue with donor restrictions
choices.explanation: Releases aren't revenue.

choices.text: As a reduction of program expenses
choices.explanation: Releases aren't netted.

choices.text: Only in the notes to the statements
choices.explanation: It's shown on the face.

mcqs.explanation: When a purpose restriction is met, net assets are reclassified from with donor restrictions to without donor restrictions.

mcqs.stem: An NFP's board sets aside $1,000,000 of unrestricted funds as a quasi-endowment. How is it classified?

choices.explanation: Only donors create restrictions.
Correct. Board designations aren't donor restrictions.
No obligation exists.
That category was eliminated.

mcqs.explanation: Board-designated endowments are net assets without donor restrictions.

mcqs.stem: In an NFP's statement of activities, where are expenses reported?

choices.explanation: Releases move resources first.
Expenses aren't split.
Correct. Expenses decrease unrestricted net assets.

choices.text: Only in the notes to the statements
choices.explanation: They're on the statement.

mcqs.explanation: All expenses are reported as decreases in net assets without donor restrictions.

mcqs.stem: For net assets without donor restrictions, an NFP has contributions of $500,000, releases from restriction of $100,000 and expenses of $550,000. What is the change?

choices.explanation: Releases increase this class.
Expenses reduce it.
Not the computation.

mcqs.explanation: Releases increase net assets without donor restrictions, and expenses decrease them.

mcqs.stem: Investment gains on a donor-restricted endowment carry no explicit donor stipulation about their use. Under UPMIFA, how are they classified until appropriated?

choices.explanation: Correct. Until appropriated for spending.
They stay restricted until appropriated.
They're net assets.
They're net assets.

mcqs.explanation: Under UPMIFA, gains on donor-restricted endowment funds are net assets with donor restrictions until appropriated.

mcqs.stem: Which set of statements must an NFP present?

choices.explanation: Correct. Including the analysis of expenses by function and nature.
More are required.
Also position and expenses.
All four are required.

mcqs.explanation: NFPs present statements of financial position, activities, cash flows and an analysis of expenses by nature and function.

mcqs.stem: Which net asset classes does an NFP report?

choices.explanation: That's the old model.

choices.text: Two: with and without donor restrictions
choices.explanation: Correct. ASU 2016-14 reduced the classes to two.
Classes are required.
That is not the model.

mcqs.explanation: NFPs report net assets with donor restrictions and without donor restrictions.

mcqs.stem: An NFP's board designates $500,000 as a quasi-endowment. How are these net assets classified?

choices.explanation: The board, not a donor, set it aside.

choices.text: As a liability to the board
choices.explanation: Not the treatment.
Correct. Board designations aren't donor restrictions.
Not a donor restriction.

mcqs.explanation: Board-designated funds are net assets without donor restrictions.

mcqs.stem: Investment income on a donor endowment must be spent on scholarships. How is it classified before it's spent?

choices.explanation: The donor restricted it.
Not the treatment.
Not the treatment.
Correct. The income is donor-restricted.

mcqs.explanation: Endowment income restricted by the donor is with donor restrictions until spent for the purpose.

mcqs.stem: An NFP incurs $30,000 of fundraising costs. How are they classified in the functional expense analysis?

choices.explanation: Correct. Fundraising is a supporting service.
Fundraising is not a program.
Costs are not netted.
Fundraising is separate.

mcqs.explanation: Fundraising is reported as a supporting service, separate from management and general.

mcqs.stem: Revenue without donor restrictions is $500,000, expenses are $450,000 and restriction releases are $40,000. What is the change in net assets without donor restrictions?

choices.explanation: Add the releases.
Releases increase this class.
Not the computation.

mcqs.explanation: Releases from restriction increase net assets without donor restrictions.

mcqs.stem: What liquidity information must an NFP disclose?

choices.explanation: Disclosure is required.
Not the requirement.
Correct. Quantitative and qualitative information is required.
Not the requirement.

mcqs.explanation: NFPs disclose financial assets available for general expenditure within one year and how liquidity is managed.

mcqs.stem: How is an NFP's investment return presented in its statement of activities?

choices.explanation: It's reported net.
Unrealized gains are included.
A separate fund is not required.
Correct. Report return net of external and direct internal expenses.

mcqs.explanation: NFP investment return is presented net of external and direct internal investment expenses.

mcqs.stem: A not-for-profit spends $40,000 on a program, satisfying a donor's purpose restriction from a prior-year gift. How is this reported in the statement of activities?

choices.text: As contribution revenue without donor restrictions of $40,000 this year
choices.explanation: The revenue was recognized when the gift was received.

choices.text: As an expense in the net assets with donor restrictions column
choices.explanation: Expenses are always reported as decreases in net assets without donor restrictions.

choices.text: No entry until the full restricted gift has been spent
choices.explanation: Each satisfied portion is released as it is spent.

choices.text: Released from restriction: a reclassification between net asset classes
choices.explanation: Correct. Satisfying the restriction reclassifies 40,000 from with donor restrictions to without donor restrictions, where the expense is reported.

mcqs.explanation: Expenses are reported in net assets without donor restrictions; satisfying a purpose restriction is shown as net assets released from restrictions.

flashcards.back: Statement of **financial position**, statement of **activities**, statement of **cash flows**, and the **analysis of expenses by function and nature**.

flashcards.front: Two classes of NFP net assets
flashcards.back: **Without** donor restrictions (incl. board-designated) and **with** donor restrictions (purpose, time, perpetual).

flashcards.front: In which class are NFP expenses reported?
flashcards.back: Always **without donor restrictions**. Restricted resources are released (reclassified) when the restriction is met.

flashcards.front: When is a gift restricted to buy a building released?
flashcards.back: When the asset is **placed in service** (absent other donor stipulations).
**Net** of external and direct internal investment expenses.
Qualitative management of liquidity + quantitative **financial assets available for general expenditures within one year**.
